answer: The shortcut is **Ctrl-q j**, and yes: `Ctrl-q` is a prefix SilverBullet reserves for [[Page Template]] use cases (e.g. `Ctrl-q q` creates a Quick Note, `Ctrl-q t` runs `Page: From Template`).

Memory for: What is the shortcut for opening today's journal page, and is its first key a prefix SilverBullet reserves for something?
[1] Keyboard Shortcuts.md (Modifier keys)
  Combos: Generally keyboard shortcuts are single stroke, however it possible to configure them as “combos” (multiple shortcuts entered in sequence). Out of the box, SilverBullet reserves two prefix keys for this “combo” use: / * `Mod-.` (so “command dot” or Mac and “Ctrl dot” on Linux/Windows), used for various [[Outlines]] related commands / * `Ctrl-q` used and reserved for [[Page Template]] use cases / * `Ctrl-q q` creates a [[^Library/Std/Page Templates/Quick Note]] / * `Ctrl-q t` runs the `Page: From Template` command / * `Ctrl-g` reserved for navigational commands: / * `Ctrl-g h` navigates to the index (home) page
  Constraints: SilverBullet is constrained in what keyboard can be used in a few ways: / * By the browser: you cannot (usually) override browser keyboard shortcuts, or at least shouldn’t (e.g. `Cmd-t` or `Ctrl-t` for opening a new tab) / * By already used keyboard shortcuts, see [[#Disabling keyboard shortcuts]] below to disable keyboard shortcuts for existing commands. / * By CodeMirror’s restrictions. There a few, here are some we know about: / * `Alt-letter` is not allowed (e.g. `Alt-a`), because it clashes with various (international) keyboards
[2] Guide/Make it your own.md (Get comfortable)
  Choose a shortcut: In Configuration, select **Key bindings** and use the filter to find a command you use often. **Journal: Today** is one option if you keep a journal. / 1. Click **+** beside the command to add an alternate shortcut. / 2. Press the keys you want to use, then press **Enter** to keep them. / 3. If SilverBullet reports a conflict, choose another combination. / 4. Click **Save and apply**, return to the editor and try your shortcut. / The command’s ⋯ menu offers **Reset** if you want its default bindings back. Save again to apply that reset. See [[Keyboard Shortcuts]] for reserved keys and shortcuts made of several keystrokes.
[3] Guide/Journal.md (Open today’s page)
  Open today’s page: Run **Journal: Today**, or press **Ctrl-q j**. The command opens today’s page, normally `Journal/YYYY-MM-DD`. If it does not exist, SilverBullet creates it from the journal template, with a bullet list ready for writing. Running the command again returns to the same page. / Write entries as bullets, paragraphs or tasks. Journal pages are ordinary Markdown pages, so you can organize their content however you prefer.
  Customize the journal: Open **Workbench: Configuration** and select the **Journal** category. Save and apply your changes there. / * **Enable journal** turns the journal commands on or off. / * **Journal page prefix** controls the names of new entries. The default is `Journal/`. End the prefix with `/` to group entries in a folder. / * **Journal tag** identifies journal pages for navigation. The default is `journal`. / * **Journal template page** supplies the initial content of new entries. / To customize  ...
Exact facts:
- [1] SilverBullet uses [CodeMirror](https://codemirror.net) under the hood, which does the majority of the keyboard handling. In addition, it allows to for customization of (most) keys on a per-command basis. When you open the [[Command Palette]], you will see the currently assigned keyboard shortcut(s).
- [1] It is by far the easiest to configure your keyboard shortcuts in the Key bindings section of [[Workbench/Configuration]].
- [1] The keyboard shortcut is then combined to e.g. `Mod-Alt-t`.
